newsitem.title: USA: American, pilots seek to reach pact by Monday.
newsitem.headline: American, pilots seek to reach pact by Monday.

text.p: American Airlines' pilots said they will attempt to reach a contract settlement with airline management before the Presidential Emergency Board (PEB) issues its report to President Clinton on Monday.

In a recorded message to the pilots, union president James Sovich said the two sides "have accepted the Presidential Emergency Board's offer to try to mediate a settlement before the board issues its report to President Clinton, scheduled for March 17."
The Allied Pilots Association said it expects to resume talks with American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, on Friday.
The pilots union's board of directors will meet in Washington March 21 for a briefing on the talks and to review the PEB's recommendations.
The PEB, which was created to resolve the dispute between the nation's second largest airline and its 9,300-member pilots union, will submit proposed settlement recommendations on Monday.

That deadline could be extended if talks between the airline and the pilots are progressing. Labor experts the PEB may delay submitting a settlement proposal to Clinton until both sides have given their tacit approval of the recommendations.
